# k0rdent_project (Resource)

A project, which is the scope most other resources in this provider are created inside.

Unlike every other resource here it takes no `project`, and its `region` isn't part of its address: it lives on the global control-plane tier and is addressed inside an organization. It's created in one region and locked to it, and every regional resource in it has to be in that region. The value it produces in `id` is what goes in the provider block's `project`, or in another resource's `project` argument.

The provider block cannot take a value that is unknown at plan time. When one configuration both creates a project and points the provider block at it, set `id` here so the value is known; a resource's own `project` argument has no such limit.

**This provider cannot create an organization.** That is an operator-plane operation and is not reachable by a tenant credential, so `organization_id` is an input. The `k0rdent_projects` data source reports it per project.

**What replaces it.** Changing `id`, `organization_id` or `region` cannot be done in place and replaces the project. A project contains the tenant's clusters, networks, subnets and API keys, and a replacement deletes it and creates an empty one. So a plan that would replace it fails and names the attribute, unless `allow_replace = true` is set on the resource. Everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Most other resources are created inside a project, so this usually comes
# first. It sits in an organization, not in a project.

resource "k0rdent_project" "production" {
  # Optional. Left out, the platform picks one. Set it if a provider block
  # here uses this project, since that needs the id at plan time.
  id = "cp-production"

  # This provider can't create an organization. Read the id from the
  # projects data source, or ask an administrator.
  organization_id = "org-ml-platform"

  # Everything in the project uses this region. Left out, it's the provider's.
  # Changing it replaces the project. `k0rdent_regions` lists valid ones in
  # `project_region_ids`.
  region = "us-texas-1"

  display_name = "Control plane production"
  description  = "Production workloads for the ml-platform team."

  # Only delete waits.
  timeouts {
    delete = "15m"
  }
}

# The value for another configuration's provider block.
output "project_id" {
  value = k0rdent_project.production.id
}

# Warn if an administrator has suspended or disabled the project. Nothing can
# be built in it then.
check "project_is_usable" {
  assert {
    condition     = k0rdent_project.production.status == "active"
    error_message = "Project ${k0rdent_project.production.id} is ${k0rdent_project.production.status}, so nothing can be created in it."
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `organization_id` (String) The organization to create the project in. A project cannot be moved between organizations, so changing this replaces it. The platform refuses to delete a project that still holds clusters, so a replacement fails until they are gone. It does not remove the project's networks, subnets or VPCs, and it does not disable project-scoped API keys: revoke those yourself. The `k0rdent_organizations` data source lists the organizations the credential can see. **Known gap.** An API key may list no organizations, and `k0rdent_projects` can only report an organization that already holds a project. So the first project in an organization takes its id as a literal. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `allow_replace` (Boolean) Permit a plan that replaces this project. Left out or `false`, a change that cannot be made in place fails the plan, naming the attribute that forces the replacement, instead of destroying the project and creating another. Set it to `true` in the same configuration as the change to let the replacement go ahead, and remove it afterwards to put the guard back. It is read from the configuration being planned and must be known at plan time. It is never sent to the platform: setting or removing it on its own is an update that changes nothing there.
- `description` (String) Free-form description. Mutable. Removing it clears it.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. Mutable. Removing it clears it.
- `id` (String) Project id, the value the provider block's `project` takes. Unique inside its organization. Omit it and the provider generates one, `tf-` and 16 hex digits, which is known only after apply, so that a create whose answer is lost can be read back rather than sent twice. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `region` (String) The region the project is created in and locked to. Every regional resource in the project has to be in this region. Defaults to the provider's `region`, and a project needs one or the other. The region has to be one that can hold a project: the `k0rdent_regions` data source lists each region's `hosts_projects`. A project's region can't change, so changing this, or the provider region it defaults from, replaces the project. A project made before regions were required reads back with none and can't be given one: leave `region` out for it. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** String length must be between 1 and 63. Must be a region id: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long each operation may take before it fails. Each operation left out defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this project.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status as last read. `active` is usable. `suspended` and `disabled` are steady states the platform can hold a project in, and are reported rather than waited out or treated as a failure.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.

## Timeouts

The `timeouts` block sets how long each operation may take before it fails:

- `delete` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone.

Each default is the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. An operation the block leaves out takes that value, so raising `operation_timeout` raises all of them at once. A value of zero or less is refused at plan time rather than read as no limit.

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_project" "example" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    delete = "45m"
  }
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The same two parts, named. Leave out organization_id and it's looked up, as
# it is for a bare id.
import {
  to = k0rdent_project.production
  identity = {
    organization_id = "org-ml-platform"
    id              = "cp-production"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The project's id.

#### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) Id of the organization that holds the project. Left out on import, it is looked up, and an id more than one organization holds is refused.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Takes every id form `terraform import` does. The first command below gives
# only the project id, which fails if two organizations use it. The second
# names the organization too.
import {
  to = k0rdent_project.production
  id = "org-ml-platform/cp-production"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k0rdent_project.production cp-production

terraform import k0rdent_project.production org-ml-platform/cp-production
```
